p0.original: 第二章 是什么蒙蔽了爱？
p0.en: Chapter two. What's the blindfolding of love?

p1.original: 是什么使我们难以体会到心中的爱？在思考这个问题时，我发现某些语言和表达方式的负面影响。它们虽然致力于满足某种愿望，却倾向于忽视人的感受和需要，以致彼此的疏远和伤害。这些语言和表达方式，我称为“异化的沟通方式”。
p1.en: What makes it hard to feel the love in our hearts? In thinking about this issue, I have found the negative impact of certain languages and expressions. While they are committed to meeting certain aspirations, they tend to ignore people's feelings and needs and to alienate and harm each other. These are the languages and expressions that I call “the means of communication that are alienated”.

p3.original: 道德评判是用道德标准来评判人，如果一个人的行为不符合我们的价值观，那他就被看作是不道德的或邪恶的。例如：“你的毛病是你太自私了。”“他对人有成见。”“这是不恰当的。”批评、指责、辱骂、归类、比较以及评论等都是在评判人。
p3.en: Moral judgment is judged by moral standards, and if a person's behaviour is not in keeping with our values, he is seen as immoral or evil. For example: "Your problem is that you're too selfish. “He has stereotypes about people. “This is inappropriate. “Censorship, blame, insults, categorization, comparison and commentary are all judges.

p4.original: 苏菲派诗人鲁米写道：“在道德与不道德的区分之外，有片田野。我将在那里见你。”然而，语言使我们陷于是非之中。它擅长将人分类，把人看作好人或坏人，正常或不正常，负责任或不负责任，聪明或愚蠢，等等。
p4.en: The Sufi poet Rumi wrote: “There is a field outside the distinction between morality and immorality. I'll see you there. However, language has put us in the middle of right and wrong. It is good at categorizing people, seeing people as good or bad, normal or abnormal, responsible or irresponsible, smart or stupid, etc.

p5.original: 我从小就学着以貌似客观的语言表达自己。一旦遇到不喜欢的人或不理解的事，就会想别人有什么不对。如果老师布置的作业我不想做，那他就“太过分了”。如果有人开车横冲到我前面，那他就是“混蛋”。同样的，要是达不到自己的期待，我也会觉得自己有毛病。我一心分析和确定错误的性质，而忽视自己和他人的需要。因此，如果女友想多一些体贴，那她就“太粘人了”。可是，如果我想多一些体贴，那她“冷漠得像个木头”。如果同事更关心细节，他就是“有强迫症”。反之，如果我更在乎细节，他就是“粗心大意”。
p5.en: I've been learning to express myself in seemingly objective language since I was a child. When you encounter someone you don't like or understand, you wonder what's wrong with someone else. If the teacher's homework I don't want to do, he's “too much”. If someone drives right in front of me, he's an "asshole". Likewise, if I don't meet my expectations, I feel like I have a problem. I am committed to analysing and determining the nature of the error, while ignoring myself and the needs of others. So, if a girlfriend wants to be more considerate, she's “too sticky”. But if I wanted to be more considerate, she was “silent as a wood”. If a colleague is more concerned with the details, he is “compulsory”. On the contrary, if I care more about the details, he is “a careless one”.

p6.original: 我相信，诸如此类的评论暗含着我们的价值观及需要。不幸的是，以这样的方式提出主张，很可能会招来敌意，使我们的愿望更难得到满足。即使他们接受批评，作出让步，通常也不是心甘情愿的。如果他们出于恐惧或内疚来迎合我们，或迟或早，我们将会发现对方不再那么友好。当然，他们也付出了代价。屈服于外部或内部的压力，很可能使他们心怀怨恨，并厌恶自己。
p6.en: I believe that such comments imply our values and needs. Unfortunately, it is very likely that such claims will be made in such a way as to attract hostility and make it more difficult to meet our aspirations. Even if they accept criticism and make concessions, they are not usually willing. If they come to us out of fear or guilt, or sooner or later, we will find each other less friendly. Of course, they have paid the price. Complying with external or internal pressures is likely to embolden their feelings of resentment and disgust themselves.

p7.original: 重要的是，在这里，我们不要将价值判断与道德评判混为一谈。什么是可贵的品质，我们每个人都有自己的看法。例如，我们也许会欣赏诚实、自由以及和平的价值。价值判断反映了我们的信念——生命的需要怎样才能得到最好的满足。看到不符合我们价值观的行为，我们可能会说：“暴力是不好的。杀人者是邪恶的。”然而，如果我们从小就学习爱的语言，我们将会直接说出我们的价值观，而不会指责他人。此时，我们就会说：“对于使用暴力来解决问题，我很担心；我主张通过其他方式来解决冲突。”
p7.en: It is important here that we not confuse value judgements with moral judgements. What is valuable quality, we each have our own views. For example, we may appreciate the values of honesty, freedom and peace. Value judgements reflect our belief in how the needs of life can best be met. When we see behaviour that is not in keeping with our values, we might say, “violence is bad. Murderers are evil. However, if we learn the language of love from an early age, we will speak our values directly and not blame others. At this point, we would say, “I am concerned about the use of violence to solve the problem; I advocate other ways of resolving the conflict.

p8.original: 语言与暴力的关系是科罗拉多大学心理学教授O.J.哈维（O.J. Harvey）的研究课题。他从许多国家的文学作品中随机节选了一些篇章，然后统计某些词语的使用频率。这些词语涉及道德评判。他的研究结果表明，这类词语的使用频率越高，暴力事件就越频繁。在一些社会中，人们习惯于将人分为好人和坏人，并认为坏人应该受到惩罚。在另一些社会中，人们倾向于围绕人的需要来考虑问题。得知后一种社会的暴力现象远少于前一种社会，我一点都不吃惊。在美国，在孩子们最可能看电视的时间段，有75%的电视节目在播放主人公杀人或暴打对方。将暴力作为节目的“高潮”是很典型的现象。看电视的人看得津津有味，是因为这个社会告诉他们，坏人应该被惩罚。
p8.en: The relationship between language and violence is a subject of study by O.J. Harvey, Professor of Psychology at the University of Colorado. He randomly excerpted chapters from literature in many countries and then counted the frequency of the use of certain terms. These terms relate to moral judgment. His research shows that the more frequent such terms are used, the more frequent the violence. In some societies, people are accustomed to dividing people into good and bad people, and they believe that bad people should be punished. In other societies, people tend to consider issues around human needs. I am not surprised to learn that violence in the latter society is much less than in the former. In the United States, 75 per cent of television programmes broadcast homicides or beating each other during the period when children are most likely to watch television. The “climax” of violence as a programme is a typical phenomenon. People who watch TV are stingy because the society tells them that the bad should be punished.

p9.original: 暴力的根源在于人们忽视彼此的感受与需要，而将冲突归咎于对方——至少大部分暴力的根源都是如此，不论是语言、精神或身体的暴力，还是家庭、部落以及国家的暴力。冷战期间，我们看到了这种思维的危险性。美国领导人把前苏联看作是致力于摧毁美国生活方式的“邪恶帝国”；前苏联领导人将美国人看作是试图征服他们的“帝国主义压迫者”。双方都没有承认内心的恐惧。
p9.en: Violence is rooted in the neglect of each other's feelings and needs and in the attribution of conflict to the other — at least most of the root causes of violence — be it verbal, mental or physical violence, or violence within the family, tribe or State. During the cold war, we saw the dangers of such thinking. American leaders see the former Soviet Union as an “evil empire” committed to destroying American lifestyles. The leaders of the former Soviet Union viewed Americans as “imperialist oppressors” trying to conquer them. Both sides have failed to acknowledge their fears.

p11.original: 比较也是评判的一种形式。在《让自己过上悲惨生活》一书中，作者丹·格林伯格（Dan Greenberg）诙谐地揭示了比较对我们的影响。他建议读者，如果真的想过上悲惨生活，就去与他人做比较。他给初学者介绍了几个练习。第一个练习是，根据当代媒体的标准，展示完美男人或完美女人真人尺寸的全身照。他建议读者先量好自己的身体尺寸，然后与照片上的美女或帅哥的尺寸做比较，并用心体会差别。
p11.en: Comparing is also a form of judgement. The author Dan Greenberg, in his book Letting Me Live a Tragic Life, is a harmonious illustration of the impact of comparison on us. He suggested that readers compare to others if they really wanted to live in misery. He introduced several exercises to beginners. The first exercise was to present a picture of the perfect man or perfect woman in the body, according to the standards of the contemporary media. He suggested that readers measure their own sizes first, then compare them with the sizes of the beautiful or handsome person in the photograph and have a different mind.

p12.original: 这个练习实现了它的承诺：在比较时，我们开始觉得自己活得很惨。此时，我们的心情极为低落。可是，翻到下一页，我们发现，第一个练习仅是热身运动。既然形体美不是特别重要，格林伯格现在请我们比较要紧的事情：成就。他从电话簿中随机挑出几个人让读者进行比较。他声称他看到的第一个名字是大音乐家莫扎特。格林伯格列出莫扎特能说的语言以及他在少年时期的主要作品。他接着建议读者想想他们现在的成就，然后和莫扎特十二岁时的成就做比较，并用心体会差别。
p12.en: This exercise fulfilled its promise: in comparison, we began to feel like we were living a miserable life. At this time, we are in a very low mood. But turn to the next page, we find that the first exercise is just warm exercise. Since physical beauty is not particularly important, Greenberg invites us now to do something more important: achievements. He picked a few random people out of his phone book to allow readers to compare. He claims that the first name he saw was the great musician Mozart. Greenberg lists the language that Mozart can speak and his major work in adolescence. He went on to suggest that readers think about their current achievements, then compare them with Mozart's achievements at the age of 12 and think differently.

p13.original: 读者即使不做上述练习，很可能也会认为比较蒙蔽了我们对人对己的爱意。
p13.en: Even if they do not do the above-mentioned exercise, the reader probably thinks that our love for ourselves is more obscured.

p15.original: 我们对自己的思想、情感和行动负有责任。可是，人们广泛使用“不得不”这一短语。例如：“不管你是否喜欢，有些事你不得不做。”显然，这种表达方式淡化了个人责任。“你让我”是人们常用的另一短语，例如：“你让我伤透了心。”此时，我们的表达方式忽视了我们情感的内在根源。
p15.en: We are responsible for our thoughts, feelings and actions. However, the phrase “must” is widely used. For example: "Whether you like it or not, there are things you have to do. Clearly, this expression dilutes individual responsibility. "You let me" is another phrase that people often say, like, "You break my heart." At this time, our expression ignores the underlying causes of our emotions.

p16.original: 在《艾希曼在耶路撒冷》一书中，作者汉娜·阿伦特（Hannah Arendt）纪录了审判纳粹战犯阿道夫·艾希曼（Adolph Eichmann）的过程。据她的记载，艾希曼及其同事借助“Amtssprache”回避责任。“Amtssprache”大意是“办公室语言”或“行政命令”。例如，如果问他为什么采取了某种行动，他也许会说：“我不得不做。”如果追问为什么“不得不做”，他就会答道，“长官命令”、“公司政策”或“法律规定”。
p16.en: In the book Eichmann in Jerusalem, the author Hannah Arendt documented the trial of Adolf Eichmann, a Nazi war criminal. According to her records, Eichmann and her colleagues have used “Amtsprache” to avoid responsibility. “Amtsprache” is intended to mean “office language” or “administrative order”. For example, if asked why he had taken some action, he might have said, “I had to do it. “If asked why “must do”, he would answer, “instructor's order”, “corporate policy” or “legal regulation”.

p17.original: 当我们根据以下理由行动时，我们也就试图回避责任。
p17.en: When we act on the following grounds, we also try to evade responsibility.

p18.en: • Driven by a force that is not clear.

p19.en: Why do you clean the room?

p21.original: ·我们的个人情况、成长历程、自我形象等。
p21.en: • Our personal circumstances, our growth, our self-image, etc.

p25.original: 为什么我要打自己的小孩？
p25.en: Why would I hit my own kid?

p28.en: Why are you cheating on customers?

p35.original: →因为你违规了，根据学校规定，我必须这么做。
p35.en: Because you're breaking the law, I have to do it under school regulations.

p36.original: ·性别角色、社会角色或年龄角色
p36.en: Gender roles, social roles or age roles

p37.original: 为什么我必须做我讨厌的工作？
p37.en: Why do I have to do what I hate?

p38.original: →因为我不仅是一个丈夫，而且还是一个父亲。
p38.en: Because I'm not only a husband, I'm a father.

p41.original: →因为吃巧克力的冲动征服了我。
p41.en: I've been conquered by the urge to eat chocolate.

p42.original: 有一次，在与家长和老师讨论回避责任所带来的危险时，一位女士气愤地说：“但有些事，你确实不得不做，不管你是否喜欢！我认为，告诉孩子有些事他们也不得不做，并没有什么不对。”于是，我请她举例说明什么事她“不得不”做，她有点不屑地回答：“这太容易了！今晚离开这里后，我不得不做饭。我讨厌做饭！我早就受够了！但二十年来，每天我都不得不做饭。即使有时累得像一条狗。因为这是你不得不做的事情。”我告诉她，听到她长期做自己讨厌的事情，我很难过。我希望非暴力沟通能帮她找到解决办法。
p42.en: On one occasion, when discussing the dangers of avoiding responsibility with parents and teachers, a woman said with indignation: “But there are things you do have to do, whether you like them or not! I think there's nothing wrong with telling the kids that they have to do something. So I asked her to give an example of what she “must” do, and she said, with a bit of disdain: “It's too easy! After leaving tonight, I had to cook. I hate cooking! I've had enough! But for 20 years, I've had to cook every day. Even sometimes tired like a dog. Because that's what you have to do. I told her I was sorry to hear her do things she hated for so long. I hope that Nonviolent Communication will help her find a solution.

p43.original: 很快，她从学习中找到了灵感。研讨班一结束，她就告诉家人，她不想再做饭。三个星期后，她的两个儿子参加了一个研讨班，这让我们有机会了解他们怎么看母亲的决定。大儿子叹道：“马歇尔，我刚和自己说，‘感谢上帝！’”看到我困惑的表情，他解释说：“也许她终于可以不在吃饭时发牢骚了！”
p43.en: Soon, she found inspiration from her studies. As soon as the seminar was over, she told her family that she did not want to cook anymore. Three weeks later, two of her sons attended a seminar, which gave us an opportunity to learn how they viewed their mother's decision. The eldest son groaned: "Marshall, I just said to myself, "Thank God! He said, "Maybe she can finally stop complaining at dinner!"

p44.original: 还有一次，我为一个学区的老师提供咨询服务。一位老师说道：“我讨厌评级。这样做不仅没用，而且学生会很紧张。但我不得不评级。因为这是学区政策。”此前，我们刚刚练习如何以负责任的方式来表达自己。我建议这位老师用以下的方式来表达：“我选择评级。因为我想……”。她脱口而出：“我选择评级。因为我想保住工作。”她赶紧补充了一句：“我不喜欢这样说。这让我觉得我负有不可推卸的责任。”我回答说：“这正是我建议你这样表达的原因。”
p44.en: Also, I consulted a teacher in a school district. One teacher said, "I hate ratings. This is not only useless, but students will be nervous. But I had to rate. Because it's school district policy. Earlier, we had just been practicing how to express ourselves responsibly. I suggest that the teacher put it in the following way: "I choose the rating. Because I want to." And she said, "I chose the rating. Because I want to keep my job. She quickly added, "I don't like to say that. This makes me feel that I have an inescapable responsibility. And I said, "That's why I suggested you say it.

p45.original: 法国作家乔治·贝尔纳诺斯（George Bernanos）有段话引起了我的共鸣：
p45.en: The French writer George Bernanos has a resonance with me:

p46.original: “我常常想，如果有一天，技术的进步最终被用来摧毁人类，那么，并非是暴行导致人类的灭亡，当然，更不能说是复仇行为使人类灭亡……人类的灭亡，却是因为现代人唯唯诺诺、缺乏责任感，毕恭毕敬地服从各种命令。我们所看到的悲剧和马上就要看到的更大悲剧，并非是世界上反抗的人、不服从的人增多了，而是唯命是从的人、听话的人越来越多。”
p46.en: “I often think that if one day technological progress is ultimately used to destroy humanity, it is not the atrocities that lead to its demise, not to mention, of course, the acts of revenge that bring about its demise... The demise of humanity is due to the fact that modern humans obey orders with all due respect and respect and with all due respect. The tragedies we have seen and those that are about to see are not the increase in the number of the world's resistance, the number of the insubordination, but the number of the people who have obeyed and who have listened.

p47.original: 一旦意识不到我们是自己的主人，我们就成了危险人物。
p47.en: Once we don't realize we're our masters, we become dangerous people.

p49.original: 我们对别人的要求往往暗含着威胁：如果不配合，他们就会受到惩罚。在我们的社会中，这是强者常用的手段。
p49.en: Our demands on others are often tacitly threatened: if they do not cooperate, they will be punished. In our society, this is a common tool for the powerful.

p50.original: 许多人相信，作为父母、师长或经理，我们的职责就是改变他人并让他们循规蹈矩。我也曾以为，作为父亲，我的职责就是管教孩子。可是，我发现，我可以提出各种要求，但无法强迫孩子们按我的期待生活。盛气凌人并无济于事。是的，我可以通过惩罚来教训他们，但如果我真的那样做了，他们迟早也会想出办法来对付我。
p50.en: Many believe that it is our duty, as parents, chiefs or managers, to change others and to keep them in line. I also thought that, as a father, my duty was to discipline children. But I find that I can make demands, but I cannot force children to live as I expected. The anger does not help. Yes, I can teach them a lesson by punishing them, but if I did, sooner or later they'd figure out a way to deal with me.

p51.original: 在第六章，我们将探讨请求与命令的区别——这是非暴力沟通的重要内容。
p51.en: In chapter VI, we will explore the distinction between requests and orders — an important element of Nonviolent Communication.

p52.original: 异化的沟通方式还与一个想法有关：有些行为值得奖励，而另一些行为必须受罚。这种想法通过“应当”这个词得到了体现，例如“他应当为他所做的事情受到惩罚”。这种想法认为有些人是“坏人”，应该通过惩罚让他们感到后悔并重新做人。然而，我相信，如果一个人选择新的生活，是为了追求幸福，而非为了逃避惩罚，那他的行为就符合所有人的利益。
p52.en: Diversion is also linked to the idea that some acts deserve rewards and others must be punished. This idea is reflected by the word “should”, for example, “he shall be punished for what he has done”. The idea is that some people are “bad people” who should be regretted and re-established through punishment. However, I am convinced that if a person chooses a new life in pursuit of happiness, not in order to escape punishment, then it is in the interest of all.

p53.original: 我们大多数的人使用的语言倾向于评判、比较、命令和指责，而不是鼓励我们倾听彼此的感受和需要。我相信，异化的沟通方式的基础是性恶论。长期以来，我们强调人性本恶以及通过教育来控制天性。这导致了我们对自己的感受和需要常常心存疑虑，以致不愿去体会自己的内心世界。
p53.en: The language used by most of us tends to judge, compare, dictate and condemn, rather than encourage us to listen to each other's feelings and needs. I believe that alienated forms of communication are based on sexual vice. For a long time, we have emphasized the inherent evil of humanity and the control of nature through education. This has led us to often doubt our own feelings and needs, so we do not want to feel our own inner world.

p54.original: 异化的沟通方式源自等级社会或专制社会，同时也支撑着它们。对于国王、沙皇、贵族来说，将臣民训练得具有奴隶般的精神状态符合他们的利益。“不应该”、“应该”和“不得不”这些表达方式特别适合这个目的：人们越是习惯于评定是非，他们也就越倾向于追随权威，来获得正确和错误的标准。一旦专注于自身的感受和需要，我们就不再是好奴隶和好属下。
p54.en: Differentiated forms of communication stem from and support hierarchical or authoritarian societies. It is in the interests of kings, tsars and nobility to train their subjects in a state of spiritual slavery. The expressions “should” “should” and “must” are particularly appropriate for this purpose: the more people are used to assessing right and wrong, the more they tend to follow their authority to obtain the right and wrong standards. Once we focus on our own feelings and needs, we will no longer be good slaves and servants.

p56.original: 人天生热爱生命，乐于互助。可是，异化的沟通方式使我们难以体会到心中的爱。道德评判就是其中的一种，它将不符合我们价值观的人看作是不道德的或邪恶的。进行比较也是一种评判，它会蒙蔽对人对己的爱意。异化的沟通方式还淡化了我们对自己的思想、情感和行为的责任意识。此外，强人所难也会造成心灵的隔阂。
p56.en: People are born to love life and to be happy to help each other. However, alienated communication makes it difficult for us to feel the love in our hearts. Moral judgment is one of them, which treats those who do not conform to our values as immoral or evil. Comparing is also a judgment that blinds people to their love for themselves. Differing modes of communication have also diluted our sense of responsibility for our thoughts, feelings and behaviours. In addition, the hard work of the strong can create a gap in the hearts and minds.
